weeks.title: Next.js App Router, Server Components & Zero-Bundle Architecture
weeks.objective: Understand React Server Components (RSC), hydration, streaming SSR, and Server Actions.

slides.title: React Server Components vs Traditional SPAs
slides.content: Traditional Single Page Applications (SPAs) ship megabytes of JavaScript to client phones, causing slow Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) and battery drain. Next.js App Router renders components on the server ahead of time, shipping clean HTML with zero JavaScript bundle overhead for static views.
slides.keyTakeaway: Keep state and heavy libraries on the server; ship interactive client components only where DOM events occur.

slides.title: Server Actions & Progressive Mutation
slides.content: Server Actions allow client forms to mutate backend state directly via asynchronous RPC calls without writing boilerplate API route handlers. Server Actions integrate seamlessly with optimistic UI updates and form validation.
slides.keyTakeaway: Server actions unify frontend mutations with backend transactions.

weeks.title: PostgreSQL, Supabase RLS & Type-Safe Database RPCs
weeks.objective: Design relational schemas, enforce Row Level Security, and write atomic PostgreSQL functions.

slides.title: Row Level Security (RLS) as Zero-Trust Data Defense
slides.content: In multi-tenant cloud applications, application-layer authorization checks are prone to developer omission bugs. Row Level Security enforces tenant isolation directly inside the PostgreSQL kernel: users can only SELECT or UPDATE rows where auth.uid() matches user_id.
slides.codeSnippet:
CREATE POLICY "Users manage own wallet"
ON public.wallets
FOR ALL
USING (auth.uid() = user_id);
slides.keyTakeaway: Enforce security at the database engine level, not in ephemeral web server memory.

slides.title: Stored Procedures (RPC) for Financial Atomicity
slides.content: When transferring virtual AED or deducting inventory balances, client-side math is vulnerable to race conditions and double-spending. ACID-compliant PostgreSQL functions wrap debits and credits in atomic transactions that automatically rollback on error.
slides.keyTakeaway: Atomic transactions prevent race condition exploits and double-spending.

caseStudy.scenario: An attacker sends 10 parallel HTTP requests simultaneously to withdraw AED 1,000 from an account holding only AED 1,000. How do you prevent a double-spend?

options.text: Check balance in Node.js memory before updating
options.explanation: Race conditions allow parallel threads to pass the in-memory check simultaneously.

options.text: Use database row locking (FOR UPDATE) or atomic single-statement updates enforcing balance >= amount
options.explanation: PostgreSQL row locks serialize concurrent updates, ensuring only the first succeeds.

options.text: Add a 1-second setTimeout delay in JavaScript
options.explanation: Sleep delays do not prevent concurrent race conditions.

quiz.question: What is Row Level Security (RLS) in PostgreSQL?
options: A physical lock on a server rack
A database engine security mechanism that filters query results based on user identity
quiz.explanation: RLS restricts which table rows an authenticated user can select, insert, update, or delete.

quiz.question: What does the ACID acronym stand for in database transactions?
quiz.explanation: ACID guarantees that database transactions are processed reliably.

quiz.question: What is a Foreign Key constraint?
options: A relationship enforcing that a column value must match a primary key in another table
A password to open the server
quiz.explanation: Foreign keys preserve referential integrity across relational tables.

quiz.question: Why should sensitive financial calculations run inside database stored procedures (RPC)?
options: They execute atomically inside a single database transaction, preventing race conditions
quiz.explanation: RPC functions guarantee atomic execution without intermediate network vulnerabilities.

quiz.question: What does database INDEX do?
options: Drastically speeds up query lookups on specific columns at the cost of slight write overhead
quiz.explanation: Indexes allow database engines to jump directly to target rows without full table scans.

weeks.title: Python Automation, Web Scraping & Scheduled Worker Crons

slides.title: Automated Web Scraping with BeautifulSoup & Playwright
slides.content: Automated scrapers allow businesses to monitor competitor real estate prices, hotel room rates, and flight seat availability in real time. Using headless browsers with Playwright bypasses JavaScript-heavy SPAs and dynamic hydration.
slides.codeSnippet:
from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright
with sync_playwright() as p:
    browser = p.chromium.launch(headless=True)
    page = browser.new_page()
    page.goto('https://dld.gov.ae/en/open-data')
    print(page.title())
slides.keyTakeaway: Headless browser automation unlocks dynamic client-rendered web datasets.

slides.title: Scheduled Worker Crons & WhatsApp Business API
slides.content: Automated Python workers running on cron schedules query APIs, detect transaction anomalies, and send automated WhatsApp notifications to executive phones in under 5 seconds.
slides.keyTakeaway: Automation bridges database mutations with instant mobile notifications.

quiz.question: What is a Cron job in Linux / server environments?

quiz.question: What is Playwright used for in automation?

quiz.question: What does HTTP status code 429 signify?

slides.title: Dockerizing Production Microservices
slides.content: Docker packages code, system dependencies, and runtime libraries into lightweight, reproducible containers. This guarantees that code executing perfectly on a developer's MacBook behaves identically when deployed to a Linux cluster in Dubai.
slides.codeSnippet:
FROM node:20-alpine
WORKDIR /app
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci --only=production
COPY . .
CMD ["npm", "start"]
slides.keyTakeaway: Containerization eliminates 'it worked on my machine' deployment discrepancies.

slides.title: Connecting Agents to Real-World Infrastructure via MCP
slides.content: Build Model Context Protocol servers exposing custom business endpoints. By registering your Python scrapers and Next.js APIs as MCP tools, autonomous AI agents can query your internal business data and execute administrative workflows on demand.
slides.keyTakeaway: MCP turns traditional backend APIs into cognitive agent capabilities.

caseStudy.scenario: Your Docker container crashes in production with 'JavaScript heap out of memory'. What is the root cause and remedy?

options.text: A memory leak caused by unclosed database connections or global arrays; profile heap dumps with Node inspect and configure memory limits
options.explanation: Profiling heap snapshots isolates memory leaks and stabilizes container execution.
Software heap limits are programmatic, not physical temperature.

options.text: Restart the container every 5 minutes forever
options.explanation: Band-aid restarts do not resolve production code leaks.

quiz.question: What is a Docker container image?
options: A standalone, executable package containing code, runtime, libraries, and settings necessary to run an app
quiz.explanation: Container images contain everything needed to run software reproducibly anywhere.

quiz.question: What is CI/CD in modern engineering pipelines?
options: Continuous Integration and Continuous Deployment for automated testing and shipping
quiz.explanation: CI/CD automates test suites, linting, and zero-downtime production deployment.

quiz.question: What is the primary role of a Reverse Proxy (like NGINX or Cloudflare)?
options: To handle SSL termination, load balancing, DDoS protection, and cache routing before origin servers
quiz.explanation: Reverse proxies safeguard origin servers from direct exposure and manage traffic.

quiz.question: What does Environment Variables (env) protect against?
options: Accidental leakage of database passwords and private API keys into public Git repositories
quiz.explanation: Environment variables keep secret credentials isolated from source code.
